title: Automated capacity decomposition with priority-aware fallback for hosted GPU pool exhaustion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up from 2026-03-01 hosted GPU exhaustion incident. This ticket captures the short-term stabilizations we deployed, the postmortem conclusions, and a set of targeted engineering deliverables to prevent similar queue buildups and to automate graceful degradation via priority-aware fallbacks.
postmortem_summary: On 2026-03-01 at ~03:12 UTC a high-volume tenant started a set of long-context streaming requests that pushed hosted GPU pools past safe operating capacity. Queue length rose rapidly and the autoscaler failed to react fast enough due to hysteresis and reliance on per-node utilization signals. Prefetching logic and KV-cache warmups amplified the tail latency, causing other tenants to experience increased throttling and 503s. We implemented an emergency manual prime and tenant soft-throttle; the cluster recovered after 27 minutes. Root causes and action items are listed below.
root_cause: Combination of (1) autoscaler thresholding that reacts primarily to CPU/GPU utilization and not to exponential queue growth; (2) sequence-length-agnostic slot packing that allowed a small number of long requests to occupy many slots; (3) prefetch/prefill behavior that created short bursts of additional load during admission; and (4) missing per-tenant soft-quotas and priority-aware admission gates.
mitigation_deployed: 1) Emergency tenant soft-throttle applied to offending tenant at 03:23 UTC. 2) Manual capacity priming + temporary increase of pool replica target. 3) Disabled aggressive prefetch for long-sequence requests. 4) Short-term runbook entry created to perform capacity priming and tenant throttles for similar incidents.
long_term_plan: 1) Autoscaler: add queue-gradient (dQ/dt) and request-latency SLO triggers so autoscaler scales on demand signals, not just utilization. 2) Packing: implement sequence-length-aware slot-packing and slow-start admission so large-context requests don't monopolize slots. 3) Priority fallback: introduce automatic fallback routing to lower-cost model variants or CPU-backed lanes for non-critical tenants when pool pressure exceeds thresholds. 4) Tenant controls: soft-quotas, tenant-level burst budgets, and clearer billing/alerts for heavy-context requests. 5) Runbook: codify rapid prime + soft-throttle procedure and test via chaos drills.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler responds to queue-gradient (dQ/dt) increases within <60s in staging and triggers a scale action in test harness
Sequence-length-aware packing reduces median head-of-line blocking by >=40% in synthetic long-seq benchmark
Priority fallback executes end-to-end: when pool pressure > 85% the system routes lowest-priority traffic to a smaller/more-efficient variant with <5% error-rate increase
Runbook updated and exercised in 2 chaos drills with post-drill blameless notes attached
Telemetry: new Grafana dashboard panel shows per-tenant queue growth, fallback events, and autoscaler triggers; alert defined for sustained queue-gradient > threshold
